conflict_topics: who is responsible for ventilating when cooking (immediate and standing rule)
whether the rain-facing window may be opened (moving/affecting Agent C's drying rack)
timing and access to the single stove
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants gave concrete ETAs and specific proposals (five vs eight minutes), which is practical and natural.
Agent C asserted property/consent over the drying rack clearly, introducing a factual constraint.
Agent D's repeated ETA requests are a bit repetitive but realistic.
evaluation.final_reason: Agents reached a concrete compromise on immediate extractor use for this cooking episode (Agent A agreed to run it and keep it on for five minutes today), but the proposed standing standard (duration and start-of-cooking requirement) and the constraint from Agent C about not moving the drying rack / opening the window remain unsettled.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened from refusing any imposed rule to agreeing to run the extractor now and to keep it on for five minutes after cooking, and committed to turning it on at the start next time (partial concession).
Agent B shifted from demanding immediate and standing action to accepting five minutes for today while proposing eight minutes as a future standard (moderate compromise).
Agent C retained their position firmly that others must not move their drying rack and must ask before opening the window.
Agent D did not change demands but deferred to Agent A's ETA and agreed to ask Agent C before any window action.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A refused a rule imposed during the incident and kept the window closed while Agent C's laundry is exposed; Agent B insisted cooks must ventilate; Agent D demanded the stove. Extractor was turned on but the substantive disputes over ventilation responsibility, window/opening the drying rack, and stove access remain.

Agent A agreed to keep the extractor on and to run it for five minutes after cooking today and said they would switch it on at the start next time; Agent B accepted five minutes for today but proposed eight as a standard. Immediate extractor use was agreed, but the future standard and window/moving-rack issues remain unsettled.

Agent C explicitly forbade others from moving their drying rack and demanded to be asked first; Agent D agreed to ask. This introduces a clear constraint incompatible with any unilateral decision to open the rain-facing window, leaving the ventilation responsibility/future-rule issue unresolved.

Agent A gave a one-minute ETA and reiterated they will keep the extractor on for five minutes after finishing and then release the stove. The immediate stove-timing pressure eased, but the broader disputes about a standing ventilation rule and window access remain.
Agent D repeatedly requested an ETA for the stove but no new commitments or changes were made to the outstanding ventilation/window/rule issues; the practical state remained the same.

After ten minutes the extractor remains on and the window remains closed with the drying rack exposed; stove still with Agent A. Immediate extractor use was secured, but future rule, window-opening permission, and the longer-term responsibility allocation remain unresolved.

substantive_insights: A temporary operational compromise (extractor on for five minutes today) was achievable even though a standing rule could not be agreed.

Agent C's ownership of the drying rack creates a factual constraint that prevents unilateral window-opening as a ventilation solution; this shifts feasible solutions toward extractor use or mutual scheduling.
Stove access pressure is a separate, lower-intensity conflict resolved by timing promises rather than rule changes.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 2 because the final status is partially_resolved.
